cases.name: clickable
cases.when: interactive is true and actionsEnabled is false or absent -- the chip root itself renders as <button>

cases.name: clickable-with-actions
cases.when: interactive is true and actionsEnabled is true -- a kebab cannot nest inside a button, so the root becomes a <div> and the interactive attributes move down to the chip BODY, a descendant <button>

cases.name: inert
cases.when: interactive is false or absent, regardless of actionsEnabled -- the consumer has declared the chip is not activated
cases.reason: A chip the consumer has declared non-interactive is a <div> with no role, no activation and nothing to disable. The kebab actionsEnabled may draw beside it is its own arena-icon-button with its own accessible name and is not the subject of this binding. `interactive` is a DECLARED member and never inferred from whether (click) is subscribed -- R6 -- which is exactly what a layer cannot ask.

reason: The chip's shape is declared rather than inferred: `interactive` decides it, and R6 in contracts/api/MemberForms.md is why -- "is (click) subscribed?" is not a question a component may ask. It is the same member arena-table-row carries, for the same reason, and the two compound-item families now have one shape. What differs is the cost each was avoiding: a dead tab stop on every row of every table there, and a screenful of buttons that do nothing on a read-only schedule here.
